sentences.en: One of the cool parts about moving to a new city or a new state or a new country
sentences.zh: 搬到一个新城市、新州或新国家最酷的部分之一，

sentences.en: is that you notice all these fascinating things about a place that are just
sentences.zh: 就是你会注意到这个地方所有那些迷人的事物，而这些事物对于

sentences.en: normal for people who have been there a long time.
sentences.zh: 在那里住了很久的人来说只是习以为常的。

sentences.en: When Chris Carlier moved from England to Japan in 2002,
sentences.zh: 当克里斯·卡利尔在2002年从英国搬到日本时，

sentences.en: there was one thing that really stood out to him.
sentences.zh: 有一件事让他印象深刻。

sentences.en: I think a lot of Japanese people go about their day and they don't really pay any attention to
sentences.zh: 我想很多日本人过着他们的日常生活，并没有真正去关注

sentences.en: Real world, life-size character costumes with sweaty actors inside.
sentences.zh: 现实世界中，穿着闷热戏服的真人扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Most people ignore them, but I always found them really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会忽略它们，但我一直觉得它们非常迷人。

sentences.en: Here in the US, mascots are used to pump up crowds at sporting events or
sentences.zh: 在美国，吉祥物被用来在体育赛事中调动观众情绪，或者

sentences.en: traumatize generations of children at Chuck E.
sentences.zh: 在查克芝士餐厅（Chuck E. Cheese）
给几代孩子留下心理阴影。

sentences.en: There are mascots for towns, aquariums, prisons.
sentences.zh: 城镇、水族馆、监狱都有自己的吉祥物。

sentences.en: Sometimes I just go to the dentist and the dentist has their own mascot.
sentences.zh: 有时我去看牙医，牙医都有自己的吉祥物。

sentences.en: There are mascots that tell people not to litter or remind them to stay quiet on the train.
sentences.zh: 还有吉祥物会告诉人们不要乱扔垃圾，或者提醒人们在火车上保持安静。

sentences.en: Everything has a mascot and anything can be a mascot.
sentences.zh: 万物皆有吉祥物，万物皆可为吉祥物。
有一个拟人化的熊吉祥物。
有一个拟人化的甜瓜吉祥物。

sentences.en: There's an anthropomorphized bear whose head is made out of a melon.
sentences.zh: 还有一个头是甜瓜做的拟人化熊。

sentences.en: His name is Melonkuma and he's the mascot of a region known for both its bears and its melons.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫“甜瓜熊”（Melonkuma），它是以盛产熊和甜瓜而闻名的地区的吉祥物。

sentences.en: And so, as Carlier adjusted to his new life in Tokyo, he started snapping photos of all these mascots he was coming across.
sentences.zh: 于是，随着卡利尔适应了他在东京的新生活，他开始拍摄他遇到的所有这些吉祥物的照片。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just realized one day I had like hundreds of pictures of mascots, so I started putting them online.
sentences.zh: 是的，有一天我突然意识到我拍了数百张吉祥物的照片，所以我开始把它们发到网上。

sentences.en: Carlier's hobby has since morphed into a wildly popular Twitter account called Mondo Mascots.
sentences.zh: 卡利尔的这个爱好后来演变成了一个非常受欢迎的推特账号，名叫“Mondo Mascots”。

sentences.en: And if you were to build a Twitter account in a lab, you could not concoct a more Vivian Leigh set of content than this Twitter account.
sentences.zh: 如果你要在实验室里打造一个推特账号，你绝对无法构思出比这个账号更具费雯·丽（Vivian Leigh）风格的内容了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's one of my favorite things on the internet.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是我在互联网上最喜欢的东西之一。

sentences.en: Twitter has been a rollercoaster ride of emotions for the past few months.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月里，推特就像是一场情绪的过山车。

sentences.en: So it's a real treat to see a picture of a manatee with a pompadour made out of cabbage.
sentences.zh: 所以，看到一张海牛顶着卷心菜做的蓬蓬头的照片，真是一种享受。

sentences.en: Usually, these costume mascots are out interacting with the world, waving at tourists and opening supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 通常，这些吉祥物会出现在现实世界中与人互动，向游客挥手，为超市开业助兴。

sentences.en: But like the rest of us, they recently had to spend a lot of time indoors in order to flatten the curve of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 但像我们其他人一样，它们最近不得不花大量时间待在室内，以平缓新冠病毒的传播曲线。

sentences.en: One mascot was making quarantine workout videos for people stuck at home.
sentences.zh: 有一个吉祥物在为被困在家中的人们制作居家隔离健身视频。

sentences.en: Another posted photo after photo of himself just staring blankly into space.
sentences.zh: 另一个则发布了一张又一张自己茫然盯着虚空的照片。

sentences.en: But around mid-March, I saw something kind of odd and very meta happening on the Mondo Mascots Twitter.
sentences.zh: 但在3月中旬左右，我在“Mondo Mascots”推特上看到了一些有点奇怪且非常元叙事的事情发生。

sentences.en: Some of the more well-known mascots were adding these similar new flourishes on top of the regular mascot costumes.
sentences.zh: 一些比较知名的吉祥物在它们原本的吉祥物服装上增加了一些相似的新装饰。

sentences.en: They were all wearing long, flowing blue wigs and colorful fish scales.
sentences.zh: 它们都戴着长长的、飘逸的蓝色假发，身上贴着彩色的鱼鳞。

sentences.en: The mascots were dressing up as the same creature.
sentences.zh: 吉祥物们把自己打扮成了同一种生物。

sentences.en: I posted some mascots dressed as a kind of mermaid-type creature with long hair and three legs and a beak.
sentences.zh: 我发布了一些吉祥物的照片，它们打扮成一种长着长发、三条腿、有喙的类似美人鱼的生物。

sentences.en: It was a mythical character called Amabie, a 174-year-old monster that has recently become the unexpected hero of the COVID era in Japan.
sentences.zh: 那是一个叫“阿玛比埃”（Amabie）的神话角色，一个174岁的怪物，最近在日本成为了新冠时代的意外英雄。

sentences.en: What's going on in this tweet here is that local mascots are now dressing up as Amabie.
sentences.zh: 这条推文里发生的事情是，当地的吉祥物现在都打扮成了阿玛比埃。

sentences.en: Amabie as a form of cosplay, a form of meta-cosplay.
sentences.zh: 阿玛比埃作为一种角色扮演，一种元角色扮演。

sentences.en: That's Matt Ault, a writer and translator based in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 那是马特·奥尔特，一位常驻东京的作家和翻译。

sentences.en: Because there's obviously somebody in these costumes who's dressed up as the regional mascot who is now dressing up as Amabie.
sentences.zh: 因为这些服装里显然有人，他们打扮成当地的吉祥物，现在又打扮成了阿玛比埃。

sentences.en: Matt wrote about Amabie for the New Yorker and is also the co-author of a book called Yokai Attack, the Japanese Monster Survival Guide.
sentences.zh: 马特曾为《纽约客》撰写过关于阿玛比埃的文章，也是《妖怪袭击：日本怪物生存指南》一书的合著者。

sentences.en: I spoke with both him and his co-author, Hiroku Yoda, in order to peel back all of the oniony history layers of this Twitter moment.
sentences.zh: 我和他以及他的合著者尤达博子进行了交谈，以剥开这个推特时刻背后所有洋葱般的历史层次。

sentences.en: Matt and Hiroku explained to me that Amabie is a creature from Japanese folklore, what's called a yokai.
sentences.zh: 马特和博子向我解释说，阿玛比埃是日本民间传说中的一种生物，也就是所谓的“妖怪”。

sentences.en: Yokai are monsters from Japanese folklore, and they've been part of the oral storytelling tradition here in Japan since before Japan has been Japan.
sentences.zh: 妖怪是日本民间传说中的怪物，自日本成型之前，它们就是日本口头叙事传统的一部分。

sentences.en: And they're basically like superstitions with personalities.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上就像是有个性的迷信。

sentences.en: Yeah, the yokai are characterization of natural phenomena or unexplained phenomena.
sentences.zh: 是的，妖怪是对自然现象或无法解释现象的拟人化。

sentences.en: Yokai is a pretty broad term that includes everything from shape-shifting demons, to cuddly animal-like creatures, to spirited inanimate objects, and also ghosts.
sentences.zh: 妖怪是一个相当广泛的术语，包括了从变形的恶魔、可爱的动物状生物，到有灵性的无生命物体，以及鬼魂。

sentences.en: It's kind of like trying to lump fairies, vampires, leprechauns, and an angry toaster into the same category.
sentences.zh: 这有点像试图把仙女、吸血鬼、小妖精和一个愤怒的烤面包机归为同一类。

sentences.en: Yokai are supernatural manifestations of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 妖怪是未知的超自然表现形式。

sentences.en: If you don't know what made that noise that went bump in the night, you blame it on a yokai.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道是什么发出了夜里的碰撞声，你就会把它归咎于妖怪。

sentences.en: Occasionally, they take the form of benevolent guardian angels, while some yokai are completely innocuous.
sentences.zh: 有时，它们以仁慈的守护天使的形式出现，而有些妖怪则完全无害。

sentences.en: One of my favorites is the azuki arai, which is a spirit that washes azuki beans, and that's it.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个是“洗小豆”（azuki arai），它是一个专门洗红豆的精灵，仅此而已。

sentences.en: But more often than not, there are malevolent beings associated with a specific place, kind of like regional ghosts or the troll that lives under a particular bridge.
sentences.zh: 但更多时候，它们是与特定地点相关的恶灵，有点像地方性的鬼魂，或者住在特定桥下的巨魔。

sentences.en: If you go to this part of the river, you might be pulled underwater by a kappa, a river goblin.
sentences.zh: 如果你去河的这一段，你可能会被河童（一种河中妖精）拉到水下。

sentences.en: If you go to this part of the mountains, you might be spirited away by a tengu, which is like a big, raven-like creature.
sentences.zh: 如果你去山的这一部分，你可能会被天狗（一种像大乌鸦一样的生物）带走。

sentences.en: The first yokai stories were told in the 8th century, but you can see the traces of yokai that stemmed thousands of years back, to Japan's native religion called Shintoism.
sentences.zh: 最早的妖怪故事出现在8世纪，但你可以看到追溯到几千年前日本本土宗教——神道教的妖怪痕迹。

sentences.en: The Shintoism teaches you basically appreciate things surrounding you.
sentences.zh: 神道教基本上教导你要欣赏你周围的事物。

sentences.en: And the things surrounding you shouldn't just be appreciated, but respected.
sentences.zh: 而且你周围的事物不仅应该被欣赏，还应该被尊重。

sentences.en: For Shinto, we believe in the nature, like a forest, mountain.
sentences.zh: 对于神道教来说，我们相信自然，比如森林、山脉。

sentences.en: It has a spirit, so we respect the nature's spirit.
sentences.zh: 它有灵魂，所以我们尊重自然的灵魂。

sentences.en: This is Izumi Hasegawa, head priest at Shinto Shrine of Shusei Inari in America.
sentences.zh: 这位是泉长谷川，美国修成稻荷神社的神道教主祭司。

sentences.en: Hasegawa says that Shinto was a religion that's so tightly woven into the fabric of Japanese society,
sentences.zh: 长谷川说，神道教是一种与日本社会结构紧密交织的宗教，

sentences.en: that it's difficult to separate where the religion ends and Japanese culture begins.
sentences.zh: 以至于很难区分宗教在哪里结束，日本文化从哪里开始。

sentences.en: Modern day, Japanese people didn't realize Shinto is our culture's basis.
sentences.zh: 现代日本人没有意识到神道教是我们文化的基础。

sentences.en: So I say it's not religion.
It's more like a way of living and culture, tradition, custom.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一种生活方式、文化、传统和习俗。

sentences.en: Hasegawa says that Shintoism is a belief system that venerates millions of deities that live all around us and impact daily life.
sentences.zh: 长谷川说，神道教是一个崇拜数百万神灵的信仰体系，这些神灵生活在我们周围，影响着日常生活。

sentences.en: After the rain stop and sun shine and then plants grow so well,
sentences.zh: 雨停了，阳光照耀，植物长得很好，

sentences.en: oh, maybe like a sun has some kind of spirits, rain, water has some kind of spirits.
sentences.zh: 哦，也许太阳有某种灵魂，雨、水有某种灵魂。

sentences.en: The growing, the productivity has some kind of the spirits.
sentences.zh: 生长、生产力都有某种灵魂。

sentences.en: These Shinto spirits are called kami, and they reside within everything,
sentences.zh: 这些神道教的灵魂被称为“神”（kami），它们存在于万物之中，

sentences.en: from the trees to the wind, even your iPhone.
Shintoism fosters the mindset that everything in the world is animated and has a spirit.
sentences.zh: 神道教培养了一种心态，即世界上的万物都是有生命的，都有灵魂。
任何东西都可以成为一个角色。

sentences.en: You have this belief system in which nearly anything can be receptacle for a deity or a soul,
sentences.zh: 你有这样一种信仰体系，几乎任何东西都可以成为神灵或灵魂的容器，

sentences.en: and many of those kami are actually personifications.
sentences.zh: 而且许多神灵实际上是拟人化的。

sentences.en: That worldview, that belief system of polytheism and animism is the soil from which Yokai emerged.
sentences.zh: 那种世界观，那种多神论和万物有灵论的信仰体系，就是妖怪产生的土壤。

sentences.en: In the beginning, tales of spirit monsters varied drastically from region to region
sentences.zh: 起初，关于灵怪的故事在不同地区差异巨大，

sentences.en: and were passed on as verbal stories with no real visual form attached.
sentences.zh: 并作为口头故事流传，没有真正的视觉形式。

sentences.en: A kapha water goblin from the south might be described totally differently from a kapha from the north.
sentences.zh: 南方的河童可能被描述得与北方的河童完全不同。

sentences.en: That is, until the Edo period.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到江户时代。

sentences.en: The Edo period, which took place between 1603 and 1868,
sentences.zh: 江户时代，即1603年至1868年之间，

sentences.en: was a time of political stability and economic growth for Japan.
sentences.zh: 是日本政治稳定和经济增长的时期。

sentences.en: And during this time, the publishing industry really started taking off.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，出版业真正开始腾飞。

sentences.en: In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries in Japan,
one of the most popular forms of book was the encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 最受欢迎的书籍形式之一是百科全书。

sentences.en: And encyclopedias are, what, full of data and information.
sentences.zh: 百科全书嘛，充满了数据和信息。

sentences.en: Well, around 1776, a artist named Toriyama Sekien came around,
sentences.zh: 嗯，大约在1776年，一位名叫鸟山石燕的艺术家出现了，

sentences.en: and he published a parody encyclopedia that wasn't full of facts at all.
sentences.zh: 他出版了一本戏仿百科全书，里面根本没有事实。

sentences.en: It was an encyclopedia of Yokai.
sentences.zh: 那是一本妖怪百科全书。

sentences.en: Sekien created a catalog that gave each Yokai a name, a description,
sentences.zh: 石燕创建了一个目录，给每个妖怪起了一个名字、描述，

sentences.en: and an illustrated image associated with it.
And this was the moment that the modern concept of Yokai emerged.
sentences.zh: 这就是现代妖怪概念出现的时刻。

sentences.en: Sekien's books were some of the first mass-produced reference images of Yokai.
sentences.zh: 石燕的书是第一批大规模生产的妖怪参考图集之一。

sentences.en: The entire nation was literally on the same page about who these monsters were and what they looked like.
sentences.zh: 整个国家在这些怪物是谁以及它们长什么样的问题上，真正达到了共识。

sentences.en: Before the Toriyama Sekien's book came out,
sentences.zh: 在鸟山石燕的书出版之前，

sentences.en: the Yokai were only drawn on the Japanese scrolls,
but the people in general cannot really see them.
sentences.zh: 普通人无法真正看到它们。

sentences.en: It essentially cemented the image of a lot of Yokai in place,
sentences.zh: 它基本上将许多妖怪的形象固定了下来，

sentences.en: and those are the images that we know today.
sentences.zh: 而这些就是我们今天所知道的形象。

sentences.en: By creating an illustrated index of them,
sentences.zh: 通过创建它们的插图索引，

sentences.en: Sekien took all these local legends and consolidated them
sentences.zh: 石燕将所有这些地方传说整合起来，

sentences.en: into a piece of national pop culture,
sentences.zh: 变成了国家流行文化的一部分，

sentences.en: in part because of Sekien's encyclopedia,
sentences.zh: 部分归功于石燕的百科全书，

sentences.en: stories about Yokai flourished during the Edo period,
sentences.zh: 关于妖怪的故事在江户时代蓬勃发展，

sentences.en: both as entertainment and as a way of explaining the many unknowns of the world,
sentences.zh: 既作为娱乐，也作为解释世界上许多未知事物的一种方式，

sentences.en: including explaining highly infectious diseases caused by invisible microorganisMs.
sentences.zh: 包括解释由肉眼看不见的微生物引起的高传染性疾病。

sentences.en: You know, today we have science to explain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，今天我们有科学来解释。

sentences.en: But back in time, there's not much information about medical.
sentences.zh: 但在过去，没有多少医学信息。

sentences.en: And that's when the Yokai comes into play.
sentences.zh: 而这就是妖怪发挥作用的时候。

sentences.en: And the plague was actually where the Yokai known as Amabie specifically came into play.
sentences.zh: 而瘟疫正是被称为阿玛比埃的妖怪发挥作用的具体场景。

sentences.en: Throughout the 19th century, cholera epidemics were sweeping the world.
sentences.zh: 在整个19世纪，霍乱疫情席卷全球。

sentences.en: And Japan was hit especially hard.
sentences.zh: 日本受到的打击尤为严重。

sentences.en: Wave after wave of outbreaks devastated the country over the course of several decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，一波又一波的疫情摧毁了这个国家。

sentences.en: And at the same time, very little was known about the disease and how to fight it.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，人们对这种疾病以及如何对抗它知之甚少。

sentences.en: According to an actual newspaper story at the time,
sentences.zh: 根据当时的一篇真实新闻报道，

sentences.en: Amabie was spotted off the coast of southwestern Japan in 1846.
sentences.zh: 1846年，有人在日本西南部海岸发现了阿玛比埃。

sentences.en: For several nights in a row, villagers could see a mysterious light radiating off the coast towards the sea.
sentences.zh: 连续几个晚上，村民们都能看到海岸向大海方向散发出神秘的光芒。

sentences.en: One night, an officer was sent to investigate the source.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，一名官员被派去调查光源。

sentences.en: He followed the light towards the water until he was greeted by a strange-looking creature who appeared out of the sea.
sentences.zh: 他沿着光向水边走去，直到被一个从海里出现的奇怪生物迎接。

sentences.en: It had the beak of a bird, long locks of human-like hair, a body covered in scales, and three legs with webbed feet.
sentences.zh: 它有鸟的喙，长长的像人的头发，身体覆盖着鳞片，还有三条带蹼的腿。

sentences.en: Kind of like a cross between a mermaid and a duck.
sentences.zh: 有点像美人鱼和鸭子的杂交体。

sentences.en: And it declared that its name was Amabie.
sentences.zh: 它宣称自己的名字叫阿玛比埃。

sentences.en: It said that there would be an abundant harveSt.
If plague should ever ravage these lands again,
sentences.zh: 如果瘟疫再次蹂躏这片土地，

sentences.en: show an image of me to the people.
sentences.zh: 就把我的画像展示给人们看。

sentences.en: It appeared in a Japanese newspaper of the era as a little article.
sentences.zh: 它作为一篇小文章出现在当时的一份日本报纸上。

sentences.en: And it was accompanied by a very charmingly crude drawing
sentences.zh: 并配有一幅非常迷人且粗糙的画，

sentences.en: that looks almost like a child might have done it.
sentences.zh: 看起来几乎像是孩子画的。

sentences.en: Because of that story, Amabie became a talisman against plague in Japan.
sentences.zh: 因为那个故事，阿玛比埃在日本成为了抵御瘟疫的护身符。

sentences.en: People would draw a picture of it and display it for others to see,
sentences.zh: 人们会画一张它的画像并展示给别人看，

sentences.en: so that Amabie would protect the world from harm.
sentences.zh: 这样阿玛比埃就会保护世界免受伤害。

sentences.en: Mythical creatures like Amabie played an important societal role within Japan in the 1800s.
sentences.zh: 像阿玛比埃这样的神话生物在19世纪的日本社会中扮演着重要的角色。

sentences.en: But by the turn of the 20th century,
Japan's relationship with its yokai began to shift.
sentences.zh: 日本与其妖怪之间的关系开始发生转变。

sentences.en: Largely because of one man in particular,
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上归因于一个人，
一位名叫井上圆了的哲学家。

sentences.en: So Inoue Enryo is known as Dr. Yokai.
sentences.zh: 井上圆了被称为“妖怪博士”。

sentences.en: If you see the word Dr. Yokai,
sentences.zh: 如果你看到“妖怪博士”这个词，

sentences.en: it sounds like he is really into yokai.
sentences.zh: 听起来他好像非常痴迷于妖怪。

sentences.en: But it was the exact opposite.
He made it his mission to displace yokai from the Japanese psyche for good.
sentences.zh: 他的使命是彻底将妖怪从日本人的心理中驱除出去。

sentences.en: Inoue was born right at the beginning of the Meiji Restoration,
sentences.zh: 井上出生于明治维新初期，

sentences.en: which was a moment when Japan began opening up to the rest of the world
sentences.zh: 那是日本在经历了数百年的闭关锁国后，

sentences.en: after hundreds of years of isolation.
sentences.zh: 开始向世界敞开大门的时期。

sentences.en: But as the country began opening up,
leaders wanted to be able to compete with Western countries
sentences.zh: 领导者们希望能够在科学、技术和军事力量方面，

sentences.en: in terms of science, technology, and military power.
So in his eyes, and in some politicians,
sentences.zh: 因此在他和一些政客眼中，

sentences.en: Japan is very behind from the West,
and they have to catch up the WeSt.
Inoue saw yokai as a crutch holding back the nation.
sentences.zh: 井上将妖怪视为阻碍国家发展的绊脚石。

sentences.en: If Japan was going to become a world power,
sentences.zh: 如果日本要成为世界强国，

sentences.en: it needed to actively embrace modern science and technology.
sentences.zh: 就必须积极拥抱现代科学和技术。

sentences.en: He felt that so long as people clung to yokai and superstition
sentences.zh: 他认为，只要人们还执着于妖怪和迷信，
用它们来解释未知事物，

sentences.en: Japan would never reach its full potential.
sentences.zh: 日本就永远无法发挥其全部潜力。

sentences.en: He went around the country finding examples of superstitions
sentences.zh: 他走遍全国，寻找各种迷信的例子，

sentences.en: or places where people said a spirit was responsible for things
sentences.zh: 或是人们声称有鬼神作祟的地方，

sentences.en: or urban legends and basically debunk them.
sentences.zh: 以及都市传说，并从根本上揭穿它们。

sentences.en: Inoue became sort of a ghostbuster.
sentences.zh: 井上成了某种意义上的“捉鬼敢死队”。

sentences.en: He created his own area of research called yokai gaku,
sentences.zh: 他创立了自己的研究领域，称为“妖怪学”，

sentences.en: and would basically go from town to town,
sentences.zh: 他基本上会挨家挨户地去，

sentences.en: being that one guy at magic shows,
sentences.zh: 就像魔术表演里那个专门拆台的人，

sentences.en: pointing out all the trap doors and mirrors in the illusions.
sentences.zh: 指出幻术中所有的暗门和镜子。

sentences.en: He used scientific experimentation to explain away
sentences.zh: 他利用科学实验来解释，

sentences.en: the natural phenomena that yokai were previously attributed to.
sentences.zh: 那些此前被归咎于妖怪的自然现象。

sentences.en: But it didn't just stop at yokai.
A lot of local customs and traditions were quashed during this time.
sentences.zh: 当时许多地方习俗和传统都被取缔了。

sentences.en: I think that movement went too far.
sentences.zh: 我认为那场运动走得太远了。

sentences.en: Our local beliefs are totally killed by the modernization.
sentences.zh: 我们的本土信仰被现代化彻底扼杀了。

sentences.en: The local deities, the Buddhist deities,
and small temples are shut down.
sentences.zh: 以及小型寺庙都被关闭了。

sentences.en: Inoue wasn't necessarily some crotchety old hater of all things wondrous.
sentences.zh: 井上并非那种对一切奇妙事物都心怀不满的古怪老头。

sentences.en: If anything, he was fascinated by the great mysteries of life,
sentences.zh: 相反，他其实对生命的伟大奥秘非常着迷，

sentences.en: what he called the true mysteries.
They were the universal conundrums that we may never find an answer to,
sentences.zh: 那是我们可能永远无法找到答案的普遍难题，

sentences.en: like what happens to us when we die or what's the meaning of life.
sentences.zh: 比如人死后会怎样，或者生命的意义是什么。

sentences.en: But he was a Buddhist and a scholar,
sentences.zh: 但他是一位佛教徒，也是一位学者，

sentences.en: and he just didn't think that monsters fell into that category.
sentences.zh: 他只是不认为怪物属于那一范畴。

sentences.en: He didn't deny all possibility of mystery.
sentences.zh: 他并没有否认所有神秘的可能性。

sentences.en: This is Michael Dylan Foster, professor of Japanese and Japanese folklore at UC Davis.
sentences.zh: 这位是迈克尔·迪伦·福斯特，加州大学戴维斯分校的日本学和日本民俗学教授。

sentences.zh: 但也有一些是无法解释的，

sentences.zh: 而那些才是我们必须去探寻的。

sentences.en: He tried to come up with solutions or some kind of answers for unexplainable things.
sentences.zh: 他试图为无法解释的事情寻找解决方案或某种答案。

sentences.en: Like, you know, like Mulder, X-File, like truth is out there.

但它们并没有完全消失，
